Attention has been drawn by Mr. Sharma to the fact that in the State, some
people are using the goods vehicles for carrying passenger which endangers their life.

Further, even

The Secretary, Department of Transport, State of Chhattisgarh, is directed to file his personal

out from the chart that the road accident data of the year 2023-24 annexed on page No.27 and 31
which goes to show that there has been great increase in the road accidents because of the
non-availability of the street light etc.

On the last date of hearing Regional Officer, Regional Office, National Highways Authority of India,
Raipur was directed to file his personal affidavit.

In compliance of the order of this Court, the aforesaid Regional Officer has filed his affidavit on
29/04/2025, the relevant portion of the affidavit is quoted hereinbelow:-
"4. That, in compliance of the order dated 24.03.2025 passed by this Hon'ble Court,
the office of Regional Officer, Nhai, Raipur, Chhattisgarh vide letter dated
22.04.2025, sent to Learned Chairman, Inter-Departmental Lead Agency (Road
Safety) Police Headquarters, Campus, Nava Raipur, Atal Nagar, District Raipur
(C.G.), has intimated and sent the reports relating to the necessary
corrective/remedial work and measures taken by Nhai on the black spots identified
by the Office of Ro and PIUs.

That, the Competent Authority has also accorded approval for initiating the bidding process of Foot Over Bridges (hereinafter referred as 'FoBs') with a total cost of Rs. 17,95,61,305/ in the stretch of Bilaspur- Pathrapali Section, with aim to avoid road accidents.

The brief detail of each location where the construction of FoBs is required is as under:
A. Km 20+100 (Turkadih village): This location falls at Turkadih village which is situated on both side of the Highway.
The population of village is 2500-3000 people on one side, there is also a Primary Government School catering to nearby villages.
There is also a Primary Healthcare Hospital.
Every day several people also cross the highway on foot for travel to local shops and village hut.
The nearest Under Pass from this location is at Km 20+700 which is found cumbersome by the pedestrian traffic.
Hence there is a necessity of FOB Of the above local pedestrian traffic.
B. Km 23+980 (Sendri Town, at grade junction):
This location falls in Sendri town which has a large population of about 5000 people.
There is a Government High School in which 3000 student's study which is a significant number.
The highway passes through the middle of the village where the residents cross the Highway on foot through of the day.
The area is accident prone and a state identified black spot as per the accident data.

There is a large market of the village to which the villagers often travel by foot,
there is also a mental hospital very close to this location.
The nearest Under Pass from this location is at Km 24+854 which is quite far away for the pedestrian traffic for crossing National Highway.
Hence it is recommended to construct a FOB at this location.
C. Km 32+300 (Madanpur village):
The location falls at Madanpur village on one side on Ranigaon village on the other.
The estimated population of both these villages is 7500 people.
There is a Government Middle School and a primary Health Care Hospital adjacent to the Highway.
Besides, every evening there is vegetable and foods mandi all along the highway.
There is large number of daily needs shops in close vicinity of these locations.
Large numbers of pedestrians' commute for the above purpose and this location is an accident-prone zone.
Further there is no Under Pass nearby this location for any possibility of channelizing the pedestrian traffic.
Therefore, a FOB is found essential at this location.
D. Km 42+660 (Melnadih & Karra village):
The total population of Melnadih and Karra villages is about 4000 people.
The villages are situated on both this side of the highway.
There is a Primary School at this location.
The local traffic police has on several instances brought attention of the Authority for safety of children going to the school by crossing the National Highway on foot.
There is also a bus stop very close to this location in which several passengers de-board for the nearby Khutaghat Dam.
The nearest grade separated Under Pass is at Km 43+500 which is significantly away from this location.

Therefore, there is necessity to construct an FOB to cater to the In The Matter Of Suo Moto Public Interest ... vs The State Of Chhattisgarh on 29 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144468946/
3 above pedestrian traffic.

sentences.text: E. Km 47+540 (Beltara Town):
The Beltara town is very large one of about 5000 residents.
At this location there is a Government High Secondary School as well as a primary health hospital for the village.
There are market / offices on both side of NH which includes Dhaba Daily Needs Shops, cloth market, Patwari office, Subji Mandi etc.
Due to large pedestrian traffic at this location, it is essential to construct a FOB at this location.
It is also submitted that there are crash barriers between Main Carriageway and Service Roads on the above locations which the pedestrians are found climbing the PGR for crossing the highway."
Learned Court Commissioner is directed to verify the averments made in the affidavit of NHAI.
The State shall pay a sum of Rs.25000/- to Mr. Ravindra Sharma, Court Commissioner, as remuneration before the next date.

It has been further pointed by Mr. Dhiraj Kumar Wankhede, learned counsel for the NHAI, that the vehicles including the Trucks, which are carrying the coal and fly ash, causes dust on the entire road because of which the road accidents are taking place specially on the roads from Korba to Raipur and Surajpur-Ambikapur.
It is further submitted by Mr. Wankhede, learned counsel for the NHAI that fly ash should be transported in capsules and not in open containers.

In view of this, Registry is directed to implead the NTPC, Seepat, District Bilaspur, through Director (Personnel) and the South Eastern Coalfields Limited, through Chief Managing Director, Seepat Road, Bilaspur, District Bilaspur as party respondents in the instant petition.

Competent authority of the both the Companies shall file their personal affidavits as to why any precautions are not being taken for the transportation of the coal and fly ash which are causing havoc due to which road accidents have increased by the next date.
Copy of this order be sent by the office of the learned Advocate General to the said newly added respondents within a period of one week.

Secretary, Department of Road Transport, shall also file his affidavit on this issue as to what measures he has taken to curb the transportation of the coal and fly ash which are being transported from the NTPC and SECL through trucks.
List it on 23rd of June, 2025.

SD/- SD/-
 (Arvind Kumar Verma) (Ramesh Sinha)
